title: Grove calibrates each maxExchangeRate against the vault's recorded current share price, so headroom is a per-Instance judgement
content:
A.6.1.1.2.2.6.1.3.7.1.1.2.4.3 sets `setMaxExchangeRate(GROVE_X_STEAKHOUSE_USDG_V2, 1e18, 1.15e6)` and annotates it: "ensures 1 share can represent at most 1.15 USDG (**current share price is ~1.00**)."

Recording the reference price alongside the bound is what makes the parameter reviewable. Without it, 1.15 is an arbitrary constant; with it, the bound is legible as *current price plus 15% headroom*, and a reader can check whether the margin is still appropriate by comparing today's share price to the recorded baseline.

Comparing across Instances shows the margin is a genuine judgement rather than a convention. The Steakhouse Prime vault allows 2.00 against a similar starting point — roughly 100% headroom. Maple syrupUSDC uses 3e6. Same control, same purpose, margins differing by an order of magnitude, with no stated rule for choosing.

A tight bound like 1.15 makes the guard sensitive: a modest corruption of the share price trips it. It also makes the guard perishable, because ordinary yield accrual consumes the margin — at plausible stablecoin vault yields, 15% is years of headroom rather than decades, and the parameter will eventually need raising for entirely benign reasons.

That is the trade-off in one line: sensitivity costs maintenance. A 2.00 bound will not need touching but will not catch much; a 1.15 bound catches more and turns into an operational obligation. Neither Instance's *Instance-specific Operational Processes* section records a review cadence, which is where that obligation would belong.
description: The USDG vault's bound is 1.15 with the Atlas noting the price is ~1.00, a 15% margin, where the Steakhouse Prime vault allows 2.00 — the same control tuned an order of magnitude differently.
